purpose: Universal severity and finding taxonomy for Vibe Coding site audit reports.

severity_levels.definition: Blocks a primary user path, exposes secrets or PII, creates auth/payment/admin risk, causes legal/compliance risk, or makes the site unusable.
severity_levels.typical_response: Stop unsafe work if relevant, report immediately, and plan a separate high-priority fix with explicit approval gates.

severity_levels.definition: Strongly damages task completion, accessibility, trust, SEO discoverability, conversion, or safe decision-making.
severity_levels.typical_response: Prioritize for the next fix prompt when within safe repository scope, or request approval if higher-risk action is needed.

severity_levels.definition: Creates meaningful friction, confusion, quality loss, or ranking/measurement weakness without blocking the path.
severity_levels.typical_response: Batch with related fixes when scope and ownership are clear.

severity_levels.definition: Local polish issue or minor inconsistency with limited user impact.
severity_levels.typical_response: Fix opportunistically only when it fits the approved scope; do not expand the task for style cleanup.

severity_levels.definition: Useful non-defect signal, opportunity, unknown, or future check that does not currently justify a fix by itself.
severity_levels.typical_response: Record as context or a future check; do not treat as a defect without stronger evidence.

rules: separate observed facts from inferred risks
label missing evidence as Unknown with a next approved step
do not cite screenshots, logs, HAR, Lighthouse, console output, or network summaries unless actually captured or supplied under the approved artifact policy
do not quote secret values, private data, credentials, cookies, tokens, auth headers, or payment data

categories.label: Technical frontend health
categories.use_when: Console/runtime errors, failed public requests, broken assets, hydration issues, broken routes/links, mixed content, compatibility signals.

categories.label: UX/usability
categories.use_when: Navigation, user path clarity, state visibility, control/freedom, consistency, error prevention, primary task completion.

categories.label: Accessibility
categories.use_when: Headings, landmarks, labels, alt text, keyboard/focus, contrast, reflow, status messages, control semantics.

categories.label: Responsive/mobile
categories.use_when: Mobile widths, touch targets, sticky overlays, reflow, mobile menus, modals, viewport-specific layout failures.

categories.label: Forms/tools
categories.use_when: Labels, hints, validation, states, consent/privacy, non-submit behavior, submit safety boundaries.

categories.label: SEO
categories.use_when: Titles, descriptions, headings, canonicals, crawlability, links, structured data, useful people-first public content.

categories.label: AEO/GEO/AI-friendly content
categories.use_when: Answerable sections, entity clarity, reliable sourcing, visible-content/schema alignment, useful summaries/FAQs.

categories.label: Copy/trust/legal-risk wording
categories.use_when: Grammar, clarity, claims, guarantees, pricing/risk wording, disclaimers, company/contact/support signals.

categories.label: Design/visual consistency
categories.use_when: Typography, spacing, alignment, state colors, component consistency, visual hierarchy, overlap, clipping, broken media.

categories.label: Analytics/conversion
categories.use_when: CTA visibility, funnel clarity, public instrumentation signals, friction, dead ends, trust blockers.

categories.label: Public UI security/privacy
categories.use_when: Exposed secrets, PII, debug output, private endpoints, auth/payment/admin boundaries, mixed content, unsafe errors.

duplicate_handling: group repeated instances when root cause and recommendation are the same
split findings when severity, user path, route, root cause, or fix owner differs
link related findings instead of copying the same evidence into multiple rows
keep regression findings tied to the original finding ID
